rounds.proof_sketch: Mutation is in gelu_kernel<half> specialization (line 43). AT_DISPATCH_FLOATING_TYPES_AND_HALF dispatches to gelu_kernel<float> for float32 input. The generic template (lines 27-37) is unmutated and handles float32 correctly. The mutated half specialization is never instantiated.
rounds.survival_reason: The mutation changes the indexing formula from '+threadIdx.x' to '-threadIdx.x' but only in the template specialization for half-precision (float16) inputs. The input specification fixes dtype at torch.float32, which causes the kernel dispatch to select the generic gelu_kernel<T> template rather than the specialized gelu_kernel<half>. The generic template is completely unmutated and computes indices correctly. Since C++ template specialization is resolved at compile time based on dtype, no runtime value change can redirect execution to the mutated code path.
rounds.kill_strategy: Unkillable under the main contract. The mutation is in dtype-gated dead code. Killing requires changing input dtype from float32 to float16, which violates the fixed input specification.
rounds.recommendations: Mutation testing frameworks should filter out mutations in code paths that are unreachable under the fixed test configuration. Template specializations that aren't instantiated for the test dtype represent dead code for that configuration. Consider testing kernels with all supported dtypes as part of the main contract rather than auxiliary testing.
